_note: Written with AI assistance (Claude Code). Generated by pipeline/flame_model/build.py; never edit by hand. The idea for this model came from a Claude chat.
label: model, not a NASA measurement
scope: Black PMMA rods only, flame spreading against the flow, at 0 g (orbit) and 1 g (Earth) only (Link et al. 2018 Tables S1 and S2). No prediction at the Moon or any gravity in between.

equations: at 0 g: u = fan; at 1 g: u = hypot(fan, earth_wind)
rate = amp * max(1 - quench_wind / u, 0) * max(1 - u / (blowoff_at_18 * exp(blowoff_o2_slope * (O2 - 18))), 0)
model.gravity_note: Trained only at 0 g and 1 g, so how the flame's own flow changes with gravity is not identified: any gravity-scaling exponent fits these data identically (team review). The model is therefore not used between 0 g and 1 g.
model.fit: robust least squares (soft L1), multi-start, all 7 parameters

earth_wind.meaning: the flow that makes orbit and Earth rates match in this model (an effective fit parameter, not a measured buoyant velocity); the interval covers the fit only. Published estimates of the buoyant flow at 1 g run 20 to 35 cm/s. The data cannot say how it changes with gravity.

leave_one_group_out.how: each of 19 orbit tests (Table S1) and each of 4 Earth rod-diameter blocks (Table S2, not individual tests) hidden in turn; the model is refitted without it from random starts and predicts it. The median is over the 87 rows where both NASA and the model have a flame; 2 rows with a NASA rate were predicted as no flame. Burn / no-burn equals the always-burns baseline, so it shows no skill.

orbit_only_to_earth.note: Trained on orbit rows only, it cannot learn Earth's gravity-driven flow. It fails, so the model makes no claim across gravity.

earth_only_to_orbit.note: Trained on Earth rows only (two flow speeds), it cannot learn the low-flow behaviour of orbit.

bootstrap.how: resample whole groups with replacement, orbit tests and Earth blocks separately, and refit; intervals cover parameter uncertainty only

remeasurement_cross_check.note: Not an independent test: our tracker re-measured the same burns (B16, B19, B12, P17) whose NASA rates are in the training table. For each step the model is refitted with that test's NASA rows held out.

caveats: A model, not a NASA measurement, fitted to NASA's published rates at 0 g and 1 g only. It makes no prediction at the Moon or any gravity in between.
Trained on orbit only, it fails to predict Earth, and the reverse also fails (validation.cross_domain).
Burn / no-burn on held-out tests (89 of 98) equals an always-burns baseline (89 of 98); it shows no skill.
The remeasurement cross-check is not independent: our tracker re-measured the same burns whose NASA rates the model trains on.
At 0 g with no flow the model has no flame at any oxygen (no diffusion-only flame); NASA's ACME BRE runs (PSI-20) burned in still microgravity air at about 26% O2 and above.
Black PMMA rods only. Oxygen above 20.9% is outside the training range.

Table S1's sub-1 cm/s flow labels are approximate: NASA's on-screen air sensor (whole cm/s) reads 0 in most low-flow steps and 2 at the 0.82 cm/s steps, so it cannot confirm them, and NASA's fan calibrations do not reproduce them (team check, docs/research/accuracy/air_display/README.md). The fitted low-flow terms (quench_wind) inherit that uncertainty.

Orbit O2 values are Table S1's labels, which equal NASA's pre-burn (initial) readings; O2 fell during each burn, so late low-flow steps ran somewhat below their label. The labels are kept as the working convention (a team check found in-burn estimates fit worse).
